title: Symmetric Tree
description:
# Symmetric Tree

Given the `root` of a binary tree, determine whether the tree is symmetric around its center.

A tree is symmetric when the left subtree and right subtree are mirror images of each other. That means corresponding mirror-position nodes must have the same value, and missing children must also appear in mirrored positions.

Example trees use a level-order display: list the root, then each existing node's left and right children in node order. `null` means an absent child; trailing nulls may be omitted. A tree node stores `val`, `left`, and `right`; tree parameters or return values in code are `TreeNode` objects.

## Example 1:

**Input:** root = [1,2,2,3,4,4,3]
**Output:** true
**Explanation:** The left side `[2,3,4]` mirrors the right side `[2,4,3]`.

## Example 2:

**Input:** root = [1,2,2,null,3,null,3]
**Output:** false
**Explanation:** The value `3` appears as the right child of the left subtree and the right child of the right subtree, so the missing children are not mirrored.

## Constraints:

*   The number of nodes in the tree is in the range `[1, 1000]`.
*   `-100 <= Node.val <= 100`.

solutions.name: Recursive Mirror Comparison
solutions.description:
## Approach

Compare the left and right subtrees as mirror pairs. Two nodes match if both are null, or both are non-null with equal values and their outer children match while their inner children match.

## Key Insight

The comparison direction crosses: `left.left` must match `right.right`, and `left.right` must match `right.left`. Comparing same-side children would check equality, not mirror symmetry.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h)

solutions.name: BFS Pair Queue
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a queue of node pairs that should mirror each other. Start with the root's left and right children. For every pair, compare null state and values, then enqueue the outer pair and inner pair in mirror order.

## Key Insight

The queue stores obligations rather than ordinary tree nodes. Each obligation says, "these two positions must be mirrors," so null mismatches and value mismatches are caught immediately.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(w)

solutions.name: DFS Pair Stack
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use an explicit stack of mirror node pairs. Pop a pair, compare it, then push the outer children as one pair and the inner children as another pair. This emulates the recursive mirror check without using the call stack.

## Key Insight

The stack and queue versions maintain the same invariant. The only difference is traversal order; the pair construction is still the source of correctness.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(h)

solutions.name: Level Palindrome with Null Markers
solutions.description:
## Approach

Process the tree level by level. For each level, record node values and explicit null markers in left-to-right order, then check whether that level list is a palindrome. Continue only while at least one real child exists on the next level.

## Key Insight

A symmetric tree has a palindromic sequence at every level only if null positions are included. Without null markers, structurally different trees can look symmetric by value sequence alone.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(w)
